why: A (universes at 0) has nineteen conjuncts on the project's f_* = Φ_*F^* (Diagram/EPLoc.pushTheta) and f^* = F_*Φ^* (pullTheta), stated for every functor Θ to ℚ of any sign. They cover: independence of the representative, for generalized isomorphisms (push) and for all generalized maps (pull); the refinement and equivalence steps; (g∘f)_* = g_*f_* for isomorphisms and (g∘f)^* = f^*g^* for all generalized maps; (f⁻¹)_* = f^*, f^*f_* = id and f_*f^* = id; the representative API (homMk_rep, equiv_rep_homMk, isEquivalence_rep_Φ); IsRefinement.isEquivalence_Φ_iff; and the two base-change lemmas in the weak fibred product, for arbitrary ep-groupoids. B states independence and both composition laws, for generalized isomorphisms only and for functors to ℚ⁺. Its pushRepB and pullRepB are definitionally Diagram.pushTheta and Diagram.pullTheta. A_to_B gets everything from pushTheta_homMk, pullTheta_homMk, pushTheta_comp, pullTheta_comp and isFunctorial_push/pullTheta, using the non-item theorem_10_3_10 to make Φ an equivalence. B_to_A takes pushTheta_homMk, pushTheta_eq_of_equiv, pushTheta_eq_of_isRefinement, pushTheta_comp and pushTheta_inv from B. Because f_* is additive in Θ (pushRepB_sub: the choice in pushforwardTheta does not depend on Θ), a functor of any sign reduces to max(Θ,0) and max(−Θ,0), so B's restriction to ℚ⁺ loses nothing. The rest of A is not a consequence of B, and is re-proved outright by local copies of the project's proofs: the pull-back claims for non-isomorphisms, the base changes, isEquivalence_Φ_iff, the representative API and f^*f_* = f_*f^* = id. On the text's sentence the two sides agree; A is more general and contains the proof's auxiliary lemmas.
